script.text:
Brain Traps & Regret – The first time I watched my investment crumble, the bitter coffee at dawn tasted like ash, and the echo of my own hesitation screamed louder than any villain’s roar.

The Anchor Trap – I once let a rival’s opening bid anchor my mind, like All Might’s shadow stretching across the city, and every subsequent offer swayed beneath that impossible silhouette, until I finally cut

Loss Aversion – When the market dipped, my chest tightened as if a storm pressed against the roof of UA’s gym, and I clutched at safety, forgetting that sometimes losing a foothold reveals

System 1 Thinking – My reflex to flash a grin like Katsuki’s when a deal appeared felt automatic, a sprinting sprint of dopamine, yet the slow, deliberate System 2 was buried under the

Availability Heuristic – After the news of a sudden crash, the scent of rain on concrete reminded me of every disaster I’d seen on TV, and suddenly every investment felt as fragile as

Confirmation Bias – I caught myself scrolling through reports that sang my strategy’s praises, like a choir echoing in a hall, while dismissing the discordant notes; I’m not sure I ever fully escaped that echo.

director.hook: Why do the smartest people make the worst decisions when the price tag goes up? It turns out your brain is wired to betray you under pressure.
director.angle: Frame this as Deku's deep-dive notebook analysis on human decision-making—connecting high-stakes anime choices with real-world psychological biases like Anchoring and Loss Aversion.
images: Cinematic moody animation of Deku writing intensely in 'Analysis for the Future' notebook under desk light, rain outside window
Stylized visual graphic showing brain pathways lighting up (System 1 vs System 2) overlaid on dark anime cityscape
Split-screen dramatic shot of characters making high-stakes trade-offs with glowing red/blue psychological bias labels
director.style: Dark Anime Noir / Atmospheric Essay Style (think Wisecrack meets lofi anime edits, moody lighting, fast-paced graphic inserts)
director.title_suggestion: The Dark Psychology of Ruinous Decisions (Why You Overthink Money)
director.reasoning: The script reads like a beautiful noir novel, but YouTube audiences will bounce in the first 5 seconds. The poetic opening is too slow for viewer retention. Furthermore, mixing random names (Raj, Sarah) with MHA characters (Mei, Jiro) weakens the niche appeal. If this is targeting the Izuku Midoriya niche, it needs Deku's distinct analytical voice and seamless in-universe flavor.
director.changes_if_revise: 1. Replace the slow poetic opening with an immediate punchy hook about brain traps and regret. 2. Remove non-anime names (Raj, Sarah, Lena) and either ground everything completely in MHA lore or keep it purely character-narrated about human psychology. 3. Structure the script into explicit psychological chapters (e.g., The Anchor Trap, Loss Aversion, System 1 Thinking) to increase watch time and pacing.
